meta.title: The World's Oldest Republic Is Smaller Than Most Cities
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note: San Marino (674) is too small to appear as its own polygon at the pipeline's 110m map resolution (confirmed absent from world-atlas countries-110m.json), so highlight stays empty every beat and a gold marker on Mount Titano stands in for it, same convention used for Transnistria/Nagorno-Karabakh.

beats.voText: This country was founded in the year 301. It has outlasted the fall of Rome, the Renaissance, and every empire that came after.
It's called San Marino, a mountain republic completely surrounded by Italy, and never conquered in over 1,700 years of existing.
San Marino calls itself the oldest continuously sovereign state on Earth, older than the Vatican, older than every modern nation.
Its constitution was written in 1600, and parts of it are technically still in force today, one of the oldest governing documents in use.
With around 33,000 people, San Marino somehow has more registered cars than residents, one of the highest car-to-person ratios on Earth.
One mountaintop, 1,700 years, and never a single conqueror. The oldest republic on Earth is barely the size of a small town. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
